text:
devon: Hey — after the OTLP exporter retry change landed yesterday I'm seeing a weird class of truncated spans show up in Tempo. Anyone seen this?

maria: Noticed a couple anomalies in trace length distribution, yup. looks like large spans are getting cut around ~65kB.

ryan: Can you paste an example span payload? is this during backfill or live traffic?

devon: Live traffic. here's a redacted snippet from our producer logs when it retries:

```
WARN 2026-02-12T22:13:01Z exporter: failed to send batch: context deadline exceeded, retrying (attempt=2)
SENT CHUNK SIZE=65536
ERROR 2026-02-12T22:13:01Z exporter: partial write, truncated payload
```

anya: Hmm 65536 scream like a 64KB chunk limit from our side or from tempo's http receiver. Could also be gzip boundary combined with retries.

samir: Tempo's ingesters accept OTLP over HTTP with max_request_bytes defaults depending on the adapter. I thought we already set max_request_bytes=1048576 for internal tenants. Maybe the change toggled chunked encoding and we lost proper content-length negotiation.

maria: I pulled a few raw spans from S3 backstore that matched those trace IDs — they show full events there. So this seems to be happening at the ingest path (exporter -> tempo), not during storage.

ryan: Could also be our batching logic splitting batches and setting content-length incorrectly on retries. If the retry sends the remainder as a standalone body but still uses the old Content-Length header it would be truncated.

devon: Repro steps I'm running: set exporter.batch.size=200, batch.timeout=200ms, then throttle tempo by dropping acks to force retries. Repro is 90% reliable.

anya: Can you share your exporter config (sanitized)?

devon: Sure:

```
exporters:
  otlp/tempo:
    endpoint: "https://tempo-internal.company:55681/v1/traces"
    compression: gzip
    retry_on_failure:
      enabled: true
      initial_interval: 500ms
      max_interval: 5s
    sending_queue:
      enabled: true
      num_consumers: 4
      queue_size: 1000

service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [otlp/tempo]
```

samir: Looks normal. Two hypotheses: 1) gzip + partial write edge case on our SDK's HTTP client where .Close() isn't flushing on connection reset; 2) Tempo's http layer rejects bodies >64KB when chunked flag is present.

maria: I dug into tempo proxy logs around those timestamps and see 413/400-ish responses for some requests, but the exporter still logs retrying as if it got network errors. The ingest-bot shows: `ingest-bot: proxy rejected request: body too large (max 65536)` in our dashboard.

ryan: That matches. So two workstreams: short-term mitigation + long-term config alignment. Short-term options: reduce exporter batch size and add a per-tenant routing policy to send large spans to the dedicated ingest tier that has higher max_request_bytes. Long-term: expose a quota/retention flag and per-route max_request_bytes so Console can surface "max event size" in the UI.

anya: For Console UX, we should show per-tenant ingest limits on the model config page and highlight when a rollout changes the exporter behavior (e.g., enabling gzip chunks). Rollout notices could include a warning "may trigger truncated spans for tenants with <64KB limit".

devon: Agreed. For immediate mitigation I pushed a patch to lower batch.max_size from 200 -> 80 which seems to stop truncation in my repro. But we need a better default and a telemetry alert for span truncation rate.

maria: We can add a metric in the exporter that emits exporter.partial_writes_total with labels {tenant, exporter, backend}. Then create an alert in Console that fires when rate > 0.1% over 5m.

samir: Also suggest adding a Tempo-specific adapter in our export router: if tenant.metadata.max_ingest_bytes < payload_size then route to "dedicated-ingest" pool or reject with a clear error. Router rules could be written like: `when payload_size > tenant.max_ingest_bytes -> route: dedicated-ingest | metric:router.routed_to_dedicated`

devon: Implementation note: computing payload_size is cheap if we sum proto bytes before compression. But with compression the final bytes on the wire differ. We should compare pre-compression size to tenant.max_ingest_bytes and also consider compression ratio heuristics.

anya: UX spike: we should add a small panel under Observability -> Telemetry -> Ingest where admins see per-tenant 'Max Ingest Size', 'Recent Truncations', 'Avg compression ratio'. That will help SREs call out bad clients.

ryan: Ops question: retrofitting Tempo config: do we want to increase max_request_bytes globally? That could increase memory pressure. Better to keep conservative defaults and route heavy producers to the dedicated pool.

maria: Agreed. Also update our onboarding docs — the quickstart that sets batch.size=500 is now risky for some tenants. Add a note: "If using Tempo backend, ensure batch.size * avg_span_size < tenant.max_ingest_bytes".

samir: I'll prototype router rule and metric, and throw a quick Grafana/Honeycomb dashboard panel for truncated spans. Can we ship exporter.partial_writes_total by EOD?

devon: I can open the PR for the exporter lib right now. Will add the metric + a WARN log with trace_id when partial write detected.

ingest-bot: deploy-batch-started: patch/exporter-metrics -> staging (sha: ab12cd9) :rocket:

maria: Nice — once in staging we'll run the repro and see metric spike. If it behaves we can roll to prod with the routing rule enabled in dark mode.

anya: For Console rollout UX: add a checkbox when enabling gzip/chunked on exporters "Show warn on tenants with low max_ingest_size" (default on). That saves support tickets.

samir: I'll also add a note for Splunk/Datadog exporters — they don't chunk the same way; might be fine, so we should document backend-specific caveats.

devon: Thanks all. Action items: 1) devon: PR for metric + warn logs. 2) samir: router rule prototype + dashboard. 3) anya/product: Console checkbox + panel spike. 4) maria: update quickstart docs. We'll reconvene after staging run. :thumbsup:
